shared_elements: curved/crescent-shaped form with a row of short parallel strokes along it (comb- or fringe-like)
repeated small motifs arranged in a row within a band
linear engraved/carved outlines on a bare stone surface
justification: The strongest correspondence is formal rather than iconographic: both surfaces stack motifs into roughly horizontal registers, and both contain a long arc bearing a row of short parallel strokes, giving a comb- or fringe-like effect. Otherwise they differ fundamentally — A consists of thin, shallow scratched/pecked outlines of what read as crescent-hulled vessels with crew strokes, while B is a carefully modelled low relief on a dressed pillar populated by recognisable animals (birds in profile, a quadruped, a serpentine form) and disc/bag-like emblems, none of which appear in A.
